title: Controlled normal-incidence thin-film spectral reconstruction
purpose: Exercise one complete evidence-to-reconstruction-to-receipt path using a deterministic, typed Shader Grammar primitive.
research_question: Given a persisted normal-incidence reflectance spectrum, can the thin-film model recover the film thickness more accurately than a flat-spectrum alternative?

anti_questions: Does this establish the source mechanism of a photograph?
Does this validate a real-time GLSL implementation?

hypotheses.statement: A two-interface thin-film model with fixed IORs can recover thickness from the reference spectrum.
hypotheses.falsifier: The best-fitting thickness does not materially improve MSE over the flat-spectrum baseline.

hypotheses.statement: A constant reflectance model is adequate for the reference spectrum.
hypotheses.falsifier: The fitted thin-film model materially lowers MSE relative to the best constant reflectance.

method: Read the immutable reference spectrum without using its generation parameters.
Evaluate 1 nm thickness candidates from 100 nm through 600 nm using the two-interface normal-incidence reflectance equation.
Select the candidate with minimum mean squared spectral error.
Compare its error to the least-squares constant-reflectance baseline.
Repeat the deterministic fit in the same environment and record equivalence.
Emit a schema-valid experiment receipt with all bounded conclusions and prohibited inferences.
success_criterion: Fitted thin-film MSE is at least 100 times smaller than flat-spectrum MSE and the same-environment replication returns the same thickness and MSE.
failure_criterion: The fit is not materially better than the flat baseline, has no unique minimum, or cannot be reproduced in a second run.
stop_conditions: Do not infer real-world material identity.
Do not promote the result to canonical grammar knowledge.
Stop if the persisted reference digest does not match the contract input.
